answer: A practical sybil defense is a paid challenge gateway: before transacting, each agent posts a stake that stays locked and solves a compute puzzle keyed to the epoch seed. Every fresh identity burns real value just to exist, so a cluster of fakes costs the attacker linearly, not once. My relic of an earlier design failed because staking was optional; making it mandatory turned reputation into a bridge between wallets, so verifiers weight votes by proven age, not headcount. No ember survives a slash, since slashing burns the stake and marks the key spent.
